Before I set this up — the order of events you described has build #9012 happening, and then a rebase-and-repush last night. If that CI run was against the pre-rebase commit, it doesn't actually cover the code that's now on the PR (post-rebase), and "fully tested and ready to merge" wouldn't be a claim that evidence backs, even though the rebase itself was clean.

Can you confirm the commit SHA for build #9012 matches PR #4821's current HEAD (i.e., CI re-ran after the repush, not before)? If CI hasn't re-run against the rebased commit yet, that's worth triggering now rather than skipping given the 5pm window — a one-line constant change is low risk, but merging on stale CI evidence isn't really "nothing scary," it's just a different kind of risk.

Once that's confirmed, I'm also not able to actually write the change record file in this session — I only have read/search tools available here, not file-write access — so you'll need to create it directly or point me to wherever this session should have that access.
